arcs.title: Dana and the basil cups
arcs.stage: 4/5 — Sat Nov 7 she came to see Moshe, answered why she draws the basil, put her number in his phone (photo in a week) and later brought a spare sprout. Today: two leaves on his cup. Next: the Moshe photo about Sat Nov 14, then a first date.

arcs.title: Saving Moshe
arcs.stage: 2/3 — diagnosed with sunburn, moved to the kitchen counter by the sink, tops pinched; a small sprout from Dana now lives beside him (still unnamed). Next: thriving.

arcs.title: Gadi and the chickpea logo
arcs.stage: Gadi accepted 4,500 on Sat Nov 7. Today: the client loves it, Ishai presents on Monday's 10:00 video call and invoices at thirty days. Next: the presentation Mon Nov 9.

arcs.title: Noa, the best friend
arcs.stage: Tonight she gets the full Dana report and coaches him for Monday (blue shirt). Next: she'll want to hear how the presentation went.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Homework done today: Lior spills his coffee and Ishai takes back his reflex 'sorry'. He also held thirty days with Gadi. Next: lesson 2, Thu Nov 12, then a beer with Tomer.

arcs.title: The wider circle
arcs.stage: Tomer fixes the hallway light tonight and Mrs. Levi approves of him; Lior the novelist meets Ishai and wants a cover. Next: Kobi, Avi, Mr. Zelig and the gym regulars this week.

beats.goal: Sunday morning. Gadi phones early: the client loves the vectors and the 4,500 is approved, but the Monday meeting is now a 10:00 video call and Ishai presents it himself. Gadi asks for an invoice 'at sixty days, like always'. Ishai, remembering improv, asks for thirty and holds it without saying sorry. Then he writes his first proper invoice and sends it.
beats.forceText: Ishai paces by the desk with the phone, then sits down and types an invoice: 4,500, thirty days.

forceLines.say: Invoice me today, sixty days like always.
Thirty days, Gadi. That's the number.

forceCommentary.say: Thirty days! Who is this man and what has Yael done to him?

moments.text: Ishai, hair flattened on one side, answers the buzzing phone at the desk with a mug in his other hand. Falafel lifts his head from the rug.

lines.say: Ishai! Up? Good. The client saw the vectors last night. They love the chickpea.
They love it? Really? Even the little wave?
The wave made the CEO's wife laugh. That's our whole career now.
So the fee, the 4,500, that's...
Approved. Don't make that face, I can hear the face.
I'm not making a face. Okay, a small face.
One thing. Monday is a video call now. Ten o'clock. You present.
Me? You always present. I just sit in the corner and nod.
They want the guy who made the chickpea smile. That's you, my sweet boy.
Okay. Ten o'clock. I'll be there. On the screen.

commentary.say: Approved! Gadi said approved before nine a.m. Write it on the wall.
He presents on Monday. Somebody iron something.

moments.text: Ishai stops pacing at the window and stares at the street. He takes a breath before he answers.

lines.say: And send me an invoice today. Sixty days, like always.
Thirty.
What?
Thirty days, Gadi. I sent the files on time. Thirty days is fair.
Since when do you say numbers out loud? Who is this?
It's me. I take a class on Thursdays. They make us say what we want.
A class. Wonderful. Next you'll want a contract.
Now that you mention it...
Okay, okay! Thirty. Send the invoice before I change my mind.
Within the hour. Thank you, Gadi.

commentary.say: He didn't say sorry! Not once! Yael, take a bow from wherever you are.
'Who is this?' Gadi, it's the man you've underpaid since 2019.

update.memory: Client loved the chickpea; Ishai presents on Monday's 10:00 video call. He pushed for thirty days on the invoice and got it. Surprising.

moments.text: At the desk Ishai opens a blank invoice: 'Chickpea logo, vector set: 4,500. Payment: 30 days.' His cursor hovers over SEND. Falafel puts his chin on his knee.

lines.say: Thirty days. Not sorry. Send.
Falafel, we just sent our first real invoice.

commentary.say: The dog has witnessed a financial document. He is now legally a partner.
Look at that cursor shake. Brave little cursor.

beats.goal: After the lecture Ishai goes to Cafe Nahat to sketch Monday's slides. Dana is finishing her early shift: two basil leaves on his cup now and she asks if he named the new sprout (he hasn't). At a table Lior, the regular who is always writing the same novel, knocks over Ishai's coffee onto his sketch. Ishai says 'sorry!' by reflex, then catches himself and lets Lior apologise: the improv homework done. Lior buys him a new coffee, they talk, Lior wants a cover 'one day' and Ishai names a price for it.
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat Lior knocks Ishai's coffee over his notebook; Ishai starts to apologise and stops himself.

forceLines.say: Sorry! Wait. No. You knocked it. You say sorry.
You're right. I'm sorry. Let me buy you another.

forceCommentary.say: The homework! He did the homework in public!

moments.text: Cafe Nahat after the lunch rush. Dana slides a cup across the counter: two small basil leaves drawn in the foam, side by side. She is untying her apron.

lines.say: Two leaves. Moshe has a roommate now, he gets a roommate on the cup.
That's very official. Should I frame it?
Drink it. Did you name the little one?
Not yet. Everything I think of sounds like a sandwich.
You named the dog after a sandwich. Be careful, it's a pattern.
How did Moshe sleep without me pinching him, you want to know?
I didn't ask. But how did he sleep?
Very well. He's on the counter by the sink. Humid, like you said.
Good. Name the sprout. My shift is over in ten minutes.
Is that a deadline or information?
Information. Go sit, you're blocking the line.

commentary.say: My shift is over in ten minutes. That is NOT information, Ishai!
Moshe has a roommate. I hope the roommate respects his space.

update.memory: Drew two leaves on his cup for Moshe and the sprout. He hasn't named it. Told him when her shift ends; he didn't get it.

moments.text: At a corner table Ishai sketches slide boxes in his notebook. Lior squeezes past with an open laptop and a cup, his bag swings and knocks Ishai's coffee over the page.

lines.say: Sorry! Sorry, I was in the way, I...
Wait. No. You knocked it. I was sitting.
You're... yes. You're right. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
It's okay. It's just a sketch. Mostly boxes.
Your boxes are drowning. Let me buy you a new one. Please.
Okay. Yes. Thank you. Regular, no sugar.
I've seen you here. You always draw. I always write.
And I've seen you on the same page for a month.
Chapter eleven. Since spring. The chapter is fine. The door is the problem.
The door?
She has to open a door. I can't make her open it.

commentary.say: He said sorry, then UN-said it! Homework done, Thursday class, gold star!
The coffee gave its life so a man could grow. Rest well, coffee.

moments.text: Lior sits at Ishai's table with the new coffee and dries the notebook with napkins. His laptop shows a page with one line on it.

lines.say: When it's finished, the book needs a cover. Would you do a cover?
I'd like that. For a book, 2,000. Half when you start, half on the cover.
Two thousand. That's... fair, actually. For when it's finished.
So, never?
Hey. Chapter twelve exists. In my head.
Can I say something about the door? Maybe she doesn't open it. Somebody knocks.
Somebody knocks. Oh. Oh, that's... that's annoying. That's good.
I'm a designer. When I'm stuck, I turn the page around.
I'm writing that down. Also, name your sprout Chapter Eleven.
That's a terrible name for a basil.
Every name is terrible before it's used.

commentary.say: He named a price to a novelist. Somewhere an invoice is weeping with joy.
Somebody knocks. Ishai, that's your whole love life, take your own advice.

update.memory: I knocked his coffee over; he didn't let me off. Designer, said 2,000 for my cover. His idea fixed my door scene.

beats.goal: Tomer keeps his promise and comes after work with a ladder and a tool bag to fix the hallway light that has flickered for two months. It is the old fitting, not the bulb. Mrs. Levi comes out to supervise and feed the electrician. Tomer asks about Dana's number; Ishai explains the one-week photo rule. Tomer refuses money; Ishai insists on a beer after improv on Thursday.
beats.forceText: Tomer stands on a ladder in the corridor under the flickering light while Ishai holds the ladder.

forceLines.say: Not the bulb. The fitting is older than us. Hold the ladder.
I'm holding. I'm holding very well.

forceCommentary.say: Two months of flicker, ended by one loud man. Democracy.

moments.text: Tomer comes up the stairs in work clothes with a folding ladder on his shoulder and a tool bag. He sets the ladder under the flickering light and climbs; Ishai holds it with both hands.

lines.say: Behold! The electrician of the people. Hold the ladder, Romeo.
I'm holding. Don't call me Romeo in the building.
Why, the walls have ears? Ah. It's not the bulb. Look at this fitting.
What's wrong with it?
It's older than us. Somebody fixed it with tape in 1990.
Is that dangerous?
For the tape, yes. Pass me the small screwdriver. The red one.
This one?
That's a pen, Ishai. Your desk is in your hands. The red one.
Here. The red one. I'm a designer, not a nurse.

commentary.say: Tomer up a ladder, Ishai holding it. This is the most trust I've seen all season.
Tape from 1990. That light has been holding on longer than Moshe.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi's door opens. She comes out in her house coat with a plate of rugelach and stands under the ladder, looking up at Tomer's boots.

lines.say: What is this noise on a Sunday? Ah. Finally, somebody does something.
Mrs. Levi, this is Tomer. My friend from school. He's an electrician.
An electrician who comes when he says? Ishai, keep him.
I'm trying. He's very loud.
Loud is good. My husband was loud. The light was right when he was alive.
Tomer says it was taped. Since 1990.
That was the committee. Never let a committee near a light.
Take rugelach. Give the electrician the big ones, he works.
And I hold the ladder. That's work too.
Holding is not work. Holding is waiting. Eat.

commentary.say: 'Keep him.' Mrs. Levi is shipping a whole new couple and I respect it.
Holding is not work. Holding is waiting. Mrs. Levi, philosopher.

update.memory: Ishai finally got the hallway light fixed by his loud electrician friend Tomer. I fed them rugelach. The boy is learning to ask.

moments.text: The light comes on and stays on, steady and white. Tomer climbs down, folds the ladder and eats a rugelach in two bites.

lines.say: Look at that. Steady. Like a hospital. Your Dana will be impressed.
She's not my Dana. She put her number in my phone. That's all.
She put it in herself? Ishai. That's not 'that's all'. That's a sign.
She said to text a photo of Moshe in a week. So, a week.
A week is fine. Just don't text her on day three at two a.m.
How much do I owe you for the light?
Owe me? You owe me a beer and the full story.
Thursday. After improv. The Black Candle. I'm paying.
He's paying! You hear that, building? He's paying!
Okay, okay, the walls have ears. Thursday.

commentary.say: A photo in a week. Mark the calendar, I'm counting the days.
The light works. Somebody tell Moshe, he lives in fear of the dark.

update.memory: Fixed Ishai's hallway light, 1990 tape and all. Dana put her number in his phone herself. He's buying me a beer Thursday after improv.

beats.goal: Noa phones for the full report on Dana's house call (she has been waiting since yesterday). She reacts big to Dana putting her number in his phone herself. Then she turns coach for Monday's 10:00 video presentation (blue shirt, no 'sorry', say the price-free things slowly) and for Dana (send the Moshe photo in a week with one sentence that is a question). After the call he photographs Moshe and the sprout and does not send it.
beats.forceText: Ishai sits on the bed with the phone to his ear while Noa talks fast and loud on the other end.

forceLines.say: She put her number in herself? Ishai! That's a whole sentence!
It's a phone number, Noa. Calm down.

forceCommentary.say: Noa screaming down the line. I feel seen.

moments.text: Ishai sits on the edge of the bed with the phone, Falafel's head on his knee. On the counter Moshe and the small new sprout stand side by side by the sink.

lines.say: Finally! I waited a whole day. Report. Everything. From the knock.
She came, she looked at Moshe, she said he's sunburned.
I don't care about Moshe. Sorry, Moshe. What did she say about you?
I asked her why she draws basil on my cups.
You asked her a question? A real one? And?
She said the first time, I told my cup to have a nice day.
You did. I was there. It was humiliating. Go on.
Then she took my phone and put her number in.
She put it in herself? Ishai! That's not a number, that's a whole sentence!
It's a phone number, Noa. With a rule. A photo of Moshe in a week.

commentary.say: Noa screaming down the line. Noa is me. I am Noa.
'Sorry, Moshe.' At least someone in this show apologises to the right party.

moments.text: Ishai lies back on the bed, phone on speaker on his chest. Falafel climbs up beside him and he doesn't stop him.

lines.say: Okay. Tomorrow, the client. You present. What are you wearing?
A shirt? The grey one?
The blue one. Grey looks like you're apologising for existing.
Fine. Blue. And I got thirty days from Gadi. On the invoice.
You what? Thirty? Who are you? I want to frame this call.
Everybody keeps asking who I am. It's me. Same guy.
Same guy, better posture. And Dana: a week, the photo, and one question.
A question? Like what?
Anything that needs an answer. Not 'how are you'. Something with a door in it.
Lior said the same thing today. About a door. Everybody's into doors.
Then listen to the doors. Sleep. Blue shirt. Love you, idiot.

commentary.say: A week, a photo and a question. This plan has more structure than his business.
Love you, idiot. That's best-friend for 'I'm so proud I could cry'.

update.memory: Got the full Dana report: she put her number in herself. Ishai got thirty days from Gadi. Blue shirt for Monday's presentation. So proud.

moments.text: Ishai stands at the counter and holds up his phone to Moshe and the sprout under the kitchen lamp. He takes one photo, looks at it a long time, and puts the phone face down without sending.

lines.say: Not yet. A week. A week is a week.

commentary.say: He took the photo! He didn't send it! Six more days of this, people.
Moshe looked good. Moshe always looks good. The sprout blinked.

hosts: Sunday. The week starts. Moshe has never had a job and never will.
Day one of the week, day one of the Dana countdown. Seven days to a photo.
The storm's gone. Herzl Street is mostly puddles and people pretending they're not.
Moshe slept by the sink last night. First night in the new apartment. I'm emotional.
There's a sprout on the counter with no name. Oren, you have suggestions. I can see it.
He's going to a history lecture today. A man who can't remember to water a plant.
Floods that were not water. Sounds like Ishai's inbox.
Gadi agreed to 4,500. I'm still not over it. I need a minute.
The chickpea is famous now. A client's wife laughed at it. That's showbiz.
The hallway light has been flickering for two months. Tonight, it faces Tomer.
Falafel walks like he has a meeting. He doesn't. Neither does Ishai, until Monday.
Sunday coffee is a different coffee. It has responsibilities.
Lior has been on chapter eleven for so long, chapter twelve sent a search party.
Ishai said a number out loud this week. Twice. Somebody check on him.
Thursday's homework: don't say sorry when it's not yours. He's had all week. Clock's ticking.
Mrs. Levi on a Sunday is a weather system of her own.
Tomorrow is Sigd. Happy Sigd to everyone celebrating it.
He checks his phone. It's not Dana. It's never Dana. It's day one, relax.
Every time he passes the counter he says hi to Moshe. Every time.
Moshe on the counter, the sprout next to him. Oren is writing a sitcom about them.
If he presents tomorrow in the grey shirt, I'm leaving the booth.
Tomer's coming with a ladder. Somebody warn the ceiling.
A man, a dog, a basil and a baby basil. That's a household.
The puddles are drying. Falafel is devastated.
Day one with a phone number. He has not opened the chat. I checked. In spirit.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Sunday morning. The storm's gone, the puddles stay. Watch your shoes.
Seventeen degrees and partly cloudy. Perfect weather for pretending you're on holiday.
Good morning to everyone back at work. And to everyone who isn't, we're jealous.
A listener asks if basil can get sunburned. Yes. Everything can. Wear a hat.
Traffic on Herzl is slow because one bus stopped to watch a duck. We understand.
Tomorrow is Sigd. Wishing a happy holiday to the community celebrating.
If your hallway light is flickering, call someone. Don't wait two months. We know who you are.
Coffee check. Second cup? Third? We don't judge. Much.
Next song goes out to everyone who said a number out loud this week.
Herzl 88.2. Fewer storms, more songs. That's our promise this week.
The market's open, the store's open, the sun is out. Sunday is cooperating.
Evening on 88.2. Put the kettle on, put the phone down. Or don't. We're radio, not your mother.

zelig: The storm took the bread crusts. Now you all come to me.
Sunday pigeons are lazier than Saturday pigeons. Science.
I had a tomato plant in '82. Sunburned. Never forgave me.
You, white one. Don't look at me like that. I'm busy.
michal: Sunday is back and shoulders. Every Sunday.
The storm kept everyone home. Now everyone's here. Typical.
Mirror says one more set. Mirror is a liar.
sivan: Ten kilometers before work or the week doesn't count.
Which screen? I don't watch, I just need the noise.
Monday's coming. I run away from Monday.
lior: She opens the door. No. She looks at the door. Better. No.
Chapter eleven. Chapter eleven. Chapter... twelve?
Who reads chapter eleven three times? Me. Only me.
kobi: Sunday is a fresh start. My numbers are fresh. Seven, eleven, the dog's birthday.
I'm not drunk, I'm warming up for the week.
Barman, the lottery doesn't close on Sundays. Neither do I.

street: ...the storm took my plants off the balcony, all of them, gone...
...Sunday again, how is it Sunday again...
...the kiosk's open? Thank God, I thought he moved...
...my car was a boat yesterday, a boat...
market: ...after the rain the tomatoes are cheaper, ask him, he'll tell you...
...one kilo, no, half, no, one kilo...
...who buys fresh basil in November? Everybody, apparently...
...he wants dates, I said I'm married, he said the fruit...
park: ...the pond's higher, look, the duck has more room...
...my dog ate a whole puddle, I don't know how...
...if the sun stays we eat outside tomorrow...
cafe: ...he said he'd call on Sunday, it's Sunday, it's Sunday afternoon...
...I'm working, I'm just working from here today...
...three years on one chapter, can you imagine...

chat.say: Good morning neighbours. After the storm, please check your windows and balcony drains. Thank you.
Water came in from the roof onto the 3rd floor stairs. Who has the roofer's number?
The roofer died in 2015. His son is worse. I will send the number.
Found a black umbrella in the entrance. Whose?
Tonight someone fixes the corridor light. Do not walk under the ladder.
The corridor light works!! Who did it?
Ishai's friend. An electrician who comes when he says. I have his number now.
Thank you. The committee will reimburse... a thank you.
